text: 吃得苦中苦，方为人上人
pinyin: chī de kǔ zhōng kǔ, fāng wéi rén shàng rén
literal: eat · can · bitter · among · bitter, only then · become · people · above · people
natural: endure the bitterest hardships to rise above others

meaning.en: Only by enduring the harshest hardships can you rise above the crowd.
meaning.zh: 只有经受住最大的苦难，才能成为出人头地的人。

equivalents: no pain, no gain
per aspera ad astra

examples.zh: 吃得苦中苦，方为人上人，年轻人要沉得住气。
examples.en: Endure the bitterest bitterness to rise above others; young people must stay steady.

examples.zh: 他常用“吃得苦中苦，方为人上人”鼓励自己熬过创业初期。
examples.en: He often uses 'bear hardship to rise above' to push himself through the start-up years.

usage.en: Motivational; some now find it a cliché that glorifies suffering.
usage.zh: 多用于励志，现在也有人认为它过分美化吃苦。

text: 天塌下来有个高的顶着
pinyin: tiān tā xià lái yǒu gè gāo de dǐng zhe
literal: sky · collapse · down · have · one · tall · one · hold up
natural: if the sky falls, a taller person will hold it up

meaning.en: Don't worry: someone more capable or senior will take care of any big disaster.
meaning.zh: 不用担心，有能力更强、地位更高的人会承担大事。

equivalents: don't cross that bridge till you come to it
let someone else worry about it

examples.zh: 别太焦虑了，天塌下来有个高的顶着。
examples.en: Don't be so anxious; if the sky falls, someone taller will hold it up.

examples.zh: 他总说天塌下来有个高的顶着，对什么都不上心。
examples.en: He's always saying someone taller will hold up the sky, and cares about nothing.

usage.en: Reassuring, or a mark of carefree (even irresponsible) attitude; casual.
usage.zh: 可作安慰，也可表示满不在乎，口语。

pinyin: zhī jǐ zhī bǐ, bǎi zhàn bù dài
literal: know · oneself · know · the other, hundred · battles · not · in danger
natural: know yourself and your enemy and you'll never be in peril

meaning.en: If you know both yourself and your opponent, you will not be defeated in a hundred battles.
meaning.zh: 既了解自己，又了解对手，打多少次仗都不会有危险。

equivalents: know your enemy
forewarned is forearmed

examples.zh: 谈判前先做功课，知己知彼，百战不殆。
examples.en: Do your homework before negotiating: know yourself and your opponent and you won't lose.

examples.zh: 教练让我们研究对手的录像，知己知彼，百战不殆。
examples.en: The coach had us study the opponents' tapes: know yourself and know them.

story.en: Sun Tzu says that one who knows the enemy and himself will not be imperilled in a hundred battles.
story.zh: 《孙子·谋攻》：“知彼知己，百战不殆；不知彼而知己，一胜一负；不知彼，不知己，每战必殆。”

date.zh: 春秋末至战国 · 前5世纪
date.en: late Spring and Autumn to Warring States, 5th c. BC

usage.en: Used for any contest, from business to sport. The original reads 知彼知己.
usage.zh: 适用于商业、体育等各种竞争。原文作“知彼知己”。

pinyin: qín zéi xiān qín wáng
literal: catch · bandits · first · catch · leader
natural: to catch bandits, catch their chief first

meaning.en: To defeat a group, first tackle its leader.
meaning.zh: 要制服一伙敌人，先抓住他们的首领。

equivalents: cut off the head of the snake
strike at the head

examples.zh: 警方决定擒贼先擒王，先抓住团伙头目。
examples.en: The police decided to catch the ringleader first, as the leader is the key.

examples.zh: 擒贼先擒王，把核心客户拿下，其他就好办了。
examples.en: Go for the leader first: win the key client and the rest will follow.

story.en: Du Fu's frontier poem advises: to shoot a man, shoot his horse first; to catch bandits, catch their king first.
story.zh: 杜甫《前出塞》：“射人先射马，擒贼先擒王。”

usage.en: Strategy advice; also used in business and sport.
usage.zh: 多用于策略建议，也用于商业、体育。

pinyin: màn gōng chū xì huó
literal: slow · work · produce · fine · work
natural: slow work yields fine craftsmanship

meaning.en: Taking your time produces careful, high-quality work.
meaning.zh: 做事慢一点、细一点，才能做出精细的好活儿。

equivalents: haste makes waste
good things take time

examples.zh: 慢工出细活，别催他，他在雕这块玉。
examples.en: Slow work makes fine work; don't rush him, he's carving that jade.

examples.zh: 慢工出细活，这家老店的手工包子要排队等。
examples.en: Fine work takes time; the handmade buns at this old shop mean a wait.

usage.en: Often said to defend a slow pace; sometimes an excuse for dawdling.
usage.zh: 常用来为速度慢辩护，有时是拖延的借口。

pinyin: huò bù dān xíng, fú wú shuāng zhì
literal: misfortune · not · single · travel, good fortune · no · double · arrive
natural: misfortunes never come alone, blessings never come in pairs

meaning.en: Bad luck tends to come in clusters, while good luck rarely repeats.
meaning.zh: 坏事常接连发生，好事却很少成双而来。

equivalents: it never rains but it pours
troubles never come singly

examples.zh: 丢了工作又摔了腿，真是祸不单行，福无双至。
examples.en: He lost his job and then broke a leg: misfortunes never come alone.

examples.zh: 祸不单行，福无双至，这个月什么事都不顺。
examples.en: Troubles come in clusters; everything has gone wrong this month.

usage.en: Often shortened to 祸不单行; the 福无双至 half is rarely quoted alone and is not always believed.
usage.zh: 常只说“祸不单行”；后半句单用较少。

pinyin: yuè mǎn zé kuī, shuǐ mǎn zé yì
literal: moon · full · then · wane, water · full · then · overflow
natural: a full moon wanes, a full vessel overflows

meaning.en: Anything that reaches its peak or fullness will soon decline; stay humble and avoid excess.
meaning.zh: 事物发展到极点就会走向衰落，要谦虚，不能过度。

equivalents: what goes up must come down
pride comes before a fall

examples.zh: 月满则亏，水满则溢，成功时更要保持谦虚。
examples.en: What is full will wane; stay humble especially when you succeed.

examples.zh: 公司发展太快，月满则亏，水满则溢，需要控制节奏。
examples.en: The firm grew too fast; what peaks must decline, so it needs to slow down.

usage.en: A philosophical warning against complacency; slightly formal.
usage.zh: 带哲理意味，提醒人不要自满，稍偏书面。

pinyin: qiāng dǎ chū tóu niǎo
literal: gun · shoot · stick out · head · bird
natural: the gun shoots the bird that pokes its head out

meaning.en: The person who stands out or takes the lead is the first to be attacked.
meaning.zh: 出头露面、冒尖的人最先受到攻击。

equivalents: the tall poppy gets cut down
the nail that sticks out gets hammered down

examples.zh: 枪打出头鸟，他不想在会上第一个发言。
examples.en: The bird that pokes its head out gets shot; he didn't want to speak first at the meeting.

examples.zh: 她业绩太好，被同事排挤，真是枪打出头鸟。
examples.en: Her results were so good that colleagues shunned her: the tall poppy gets cut down.

usage.en: Often an excuse for keeping a low profile; casual.
usage.zh: 常用作低调自保的理由，口语。

pinyin: chū tóu de chuán zi xiān làn
literal: stick out · head · 's · rafter · first · rot
natural: the rafter that sticks out rots first

meaning.en: Whoever sticks out from the crowd is the first to suffer.
meaning.zh: 露头冒尖的人最先遭殃。

equivalents: the tall poppy gets cut down

examples.zh: 出头的椽子先烂，在单位还是低调点好。
examples.en: The rafter that sticks out rots first; better keep a low profile at work.

examples.zh: 他明白出头的椽子先烂，所以从不抢功。
examples.en: He knows the protruding rafter rots first, so he never takes credit.

usage.en: Folk wisdom for lying low; often paired with 枪打出头鸟.
usage.zh: 民间处世之语，常与“枪打出头鸟”并用。

pinyin: mù xiù yú lín, fēng bì cuī zhī
literal: tree · tower · over · forest, wind · surely · break · it
natural: a tree that towers above the forest will be broken by the wind

meaning.en: Those who rise above their peers attract envy and attacks.
meaning.zh: 才华、地位超出众人，就容易招来嫉妒和打击。

equivalents: the tall poppy gets cut down

examples.zh: 木秀于林，风必摧之，他在公司处处谨慎。
examples.en: A tree that towers above the forest is snapped by the wind; he is cautious everywhere in the company.

examples.zh: 木秀于林，风必摧之，太出风头未必是好事。
examples.en: The tallest tree faces the wind; standing out isn't always good.

story.en: Li Kang writes that a tree standing tall in the forest will be broken by the wind, a mound rising from the bank will be washed away by the current, and a man whose conduct exceeds others will be condemned by the crowd.
story.zh: 《运命论》：“木秀于林，风必摧之；堆出于岸，流必湍之；行高于人，众必非之。”

usage.en: Literary register; warns of the cost of standing out.
usage.zh: 文言色彩，提醒出众的代价。

pinyin: lín zi dà le, shén me niǎo dōu yǒu
literal: forest · big · (particle), what · bird · all · have
natural: in a big forest you'll find every kind of bird

meaning.en: In a large group you will find all sorts of people, including some bad ones.
meaning.zh: 人多了，什么样的人都会有，包括不好的人。

equivalents: there's a black sheep in every flock
you get all sorts

examples.zh: 林子大了，什么鸟都有，网上遇到怪人别生气。
examples.en: In a big forest you get every kind of bird; don't get angry at oddballs online.

examples.zh: 公司这么大，林子大了，什么鸟都有。
examples.en: The company is huge, so you get all sorts of characters.

usage.en: Often a shrug at people behaving badly; casual, slightly sardonic.
usage.zh: 多用于对不良行为的无奈感叹，口语，略带讽刺。

text: 一粒老鼠屎，坏了一锅粥
pinyin: yī lì lǎo shǔ shǐ, huài le yī guō zhōu
variants: 一颗老鼠屎，坏了一锅粥
一粒老鼠屎，坏了一锅汤
literal: one · grain · mouse · dropping, spoil · (particle) · one · pot · porridge
natural: one mouse dropping spoils the whole pot of soup

meaning.en: One bad element can ruin the whole group or enterprise.
meaning.zh: 一个坏分子可以毁掉整个集体或整件事。

equivalents: one bad apple spoils the barrel
a rotten apple spoils the barrel

examples.zh: 一粒老鼠屎，坏了一锅汤，一个人违规，全队受罚。
examples.en: One mouse dropping spoils the whole pot of soup: one person broke the rules, the whole team is punished.

examples.zh: 别让他进团队，一粒老鼠屎，坏了一锅汤。
examples.en: Don't let him join; one bad apple spoils the barrel.

usage.en: Describes a troublemaker; the measure word 粒/颗 and 汤/粥 vary.
usage.zh: 指搅坏整体的人，量词“粒/颗”和“汤/粥”可换。

text: 一朝被蛇咬，十年怕井绳
pinyin: yī zhāo bèi shé yǎo, shí nián pà jǐng shéng
variants: 一年被蛇咬，十年怕井绳
literal: one · morning · by · snake · bitten, ten · years · fear · well · rope
natural: bitten by a snake once, you fear a well rope for ten years

meaning.en: Someone who has had a bad experience stays fearful of anything resembling it.
meaning.zh: 被蛇咬过一次，以后看到井绳也害怕；比喻经历过一次挫折，以后就非常胆小。

equivalents: once bitten, twice shy
a burnt child dreads the fire

examples.zh: 他被骗过一次，现在一朝被蛇咬，十年怕井绳，不敢再投资了。
examples.en: He was conned once; now, once bitten twice shy, he dares not invest again.

examples.zh: 一朝被蛇咬，十年怕井绳，她分手后很怕再谈恋爱。
examples.en: Bitten once, she fears the well rope for years; after the break-up she dreads another relationship.

usage.en: Used to explain over-cautious behaviour; neutral to slightly sympathetic.
usage.zh: 用来解释过分谨慎的行为，中性或略带同情。

pinyin: bù zhuàng nán qiáng bù huí tóu
literal: not · hit · south · wall · not · turn · head
natural: won't turn back until he hits the south wall

meaning.en: To stubbornly press on until failure forces you to stop.
meaning.zh: 固执己见，不到碰壁绝不罢休。

equivalents: he won't stop until he hits a brick wall
stubborn as a mule

examples.zh: 你这人真是不撞南墙不回头，劝了多少遍都不听。
examples.en: You really won't turn back till you hit the wall; you ignore every warning.

examples.zh: 他不撞南墙不回头，非要自己试一试。
examples.en: He won't give up until he's hit the wall; he insists on trying for himself.

usage.en: Mild reproach of stubbornness; casual.
usage.zh: 轻微责备固执，口语。

pinyin: bù dào cháng chéng fēi hǎo hàn
literal: not · reach · Great Wall · not · true · hero
natural: one who hasn't reached the Great Wall is no hero

meaning.en: A true person must see a goal through; also said of climbing the Great Wall.
meaning.zh: 不坚持到底、达到目标，就不算英雄；也指登上长城才算好汉。

equivalents: no pain, no gain
go the whole way

examples.zh: 不到长城非好汉，我们爬到了烽火台。
examples.en: One who hasn't reached the Great Wall is no hero; we climbed up to the beacon tower.

examples.zh: 不到长城非好汉，这次马拉松我一定跑完。
examples.en: No true hero quits before the Great Wall; I'll finish this marathon.

story.en: Mao Zedong wrote this poem in 1935 on the Long March, looking at the geese flying south.
story.zh: 《清平乐·六盘山》：“不到长城非好汉，屈指行程二万。”

usage.en: Quoted from Mao's poem; used for perseverance or on a Great Wall visit.
usage.zh: 出自毛泽东词，用于鼓励坚持或登长城时。

text: 没有金刚钻，别揽瓷器活
pinyin: méi yǒu jīn gāng zuàn, bié lǎn cí qì huó
variants: 没有金刚钻，不揽瓷器活
literal: not · have · diamond · drill, don't · take on · porcelain · job
natural: don't take on porcelain repair without a diamond drill

meaning.en: Don't take on a job unless you have the skills for it.
meaning.zh: 没有相应的本事，就不要接手难做的工作。

equivalents: don't bite off more than you can chew
a bad workman blames his tools

examples.zh: 没有金刚钻，别揽瓷器活，不会装修就别接单。
examples.en: Without a diamond drill, don't take the porcelain job; if you can't renovate, don't accept orders.

examples.zh: 他不懂技术还接了这个项目，真是没有金刚钻，别揽瓷器活。
examples.en: He knew no tech yet took the project; no diamond drill, no porcelain job.

usage.en: Warning against overreaching; the second half is often dropped.
usage.zh: 告诫不要不自量力，常只说前半句。

pinyin: tiān xià méi yǒu miǎn fèi de wǔ cān
literal: under heaven · there is no · free · 's · lunch
natural: there is no such thing as a free lunch

meaning.en: Everything has a price; nothing is truly free.
meaning.zh: 任何好处都有代价，没有白得的东西。

equivalents: there's no such thing as a free lunch
there's no free lunch

examples.zh: 天下没有免费的午餐，这么低的价格肯定有陷阱。
examples.en: There's no free lunch; a price this low must hide a catch.

examples.zh: 天下没有免费的午餐，别轻信推销电话。
examples.en: Nothing comes free; don't trust cold calls.

usage.en: A calque of the English saying, now fully natural in Chinese.
usage.zh: 译自英语谚语，现已成为汉语常用说法。

pinyin: wàn shì kāi tóu nán
literal: ten thousand · things · begin · hard
natural: every start is hard

meaning.en: Beginning anything is the hardest part.
meaning.zh: 任何事情刚开始时都是最困难的。

equivalents: the first step is the hardest
well begun is half done

examples.zh: 万事开头难，坚持一周就会习惯早起。
examples.en: Starting is always the hardest; stick at it for a week and early rising becomes a habit.

examples.zh: 万事开头难，公司前三个月最艰苦。
examples.en: Every beginning is hard, and the first three months were the toughest.

usage.en: Encouragement for beginners; often followed by 但只要开始了就好办.
usage.zh: 用来鼓励新手，后面常接“只要开始就好办”。

pinyin: rén suàn bù rú tiān suàn
literal: human · calculate · not · as good as · heaven · calculate
natural: human calculation can't match heaven's

meaning.en: However well you plan, fate may overturn it.
meaning.zh: 人再怎么精心谋划，也敌不过无法预料的天意。

equivalents: man proposes, God disposes
the best-laid plans of mice and men

examples.zh: 计划得再周密，人算不如天算，航班还是取消了。
examples.en: However careful the plan, man proposes and heaven disposes; the flight was cancelled.

examples.zh: 人算不如天算，他精心布局还是输了。
examples.en: Human calculation cannot match heaven's; for all his scheming he lost.

usage.en: Said with a sigh after plans fall through.
usage.zh: 计划落空后常带叹息地说。

pinyin: rén wú wán rén, jīn wú zú chì
literal: person · no · perfect · person, gold · no · fully · red (pure)
natural: nobody is perfect, no gold is pure

meaning.en: No one is flawless, just as no gold is one hundred per cent pure.
meaning.zh: 人没有十全十美的，就像金子没有纯度百分之百的。

equivalents: nobody is perfect
to err is human

examples.zh: 人无完人，金无足赤，别对同事要求太苛刻。
examples.en: Nobody's perfect; don't be too harsh on colleagues.

examples.zh: 人无完人，金无足赤，他有缺点但很能干。
examples.en: Nobody is flawless; he has faults, but he's capable.

usage.en: Used to forgive faults; the half 金无足赤 is also quoted alone.
usage.zh: 用来宽容缺点，“金无足赤”也可单说。

pinyin: chǐ yǒu suǒ duǎn, cùn yǒu suǒ cháng
literal: foot · has · what · short, inch · has · what · long
natural: a foot has its shortcomings, an inch its strengths

meaning.en: Everyone and everything has strengths and weaknesses relative to others.
meaning.zh: 尺虽长也有不足的地方，寸虽短也有胜过尺的地方；比喻人各有长短。

equivalents: everyone has their strengths and weaknesses
every man has his strong points

examples.zh: 尺有所短，寸有所长，每个人都有值得学习的地方。
examples.en: Everyone has weak and strong points; each has something to learn from.

examples.zh: 他数学不好，但画画出色，尺有所短，寸有所长。
examples.en: He's weak at maths but excels at drawing; everyone has strengths and weaknesses.

story.en: Qu Yuan, in doubt, asks the diviner Zheng Zhanyin for advice; the diviner replies that a foot may be too short and an inch too long, things have limits and wisdom has gaps.
story.zh: 《卜居》：“夫尺有所短，寸有所长，物有所不足，智有所不明。”传为屈原所作。

date.zh: 战国 · 前3世纪（传屈原作）
date.en: Warring States, 3rd c. BC (traditionally Qu Yuan)

usage.en: Said to encourage humility and appreciate others' strengths; formal or written register.
usage.zh: 劝人谦虚、看到别人的长处，偏书面。

text: 若要人不知，除非己莫为
pinyin: ruò yào rén bù zhī, chú fēi jǐ mò wéi
literal: if · want · others · not · know, unless · oneself · not · do
natural: if you don't want people to know, don't do it

meaning.en: Secrets get out: if you don't want others to know, don't do it in the first place.
meaning.zh: 不想让别人知道，最好自己不要去做。

equivalents: murder will out
what's done in the dark comes to light

examples.zh: 若要人不知，除非己莫为，做了坏事总会败露。
examples.en: If you don't want people to know, don't do it; wrongdoing always comes out.

examples.zh: 他挪用公款被查，真是若要人不知，除非己莫为。
examples.en: He was caught misusing funds; if you don't want it known, don't do it.

usage.en: A warning, often to someone concealing wrongdoing; the next line is 要得人不闻，除非己莫言 in some versions.
usage.zh: 多用于告诫有隐瞒坏事的人。

story.en: Mei Cheng warned the King of Wu against rebellion, saying that if you do not want people to know, the best way is not to do it. The popular line is a rewording.
story.zh: 枚乘上书谏吴王谋反，称“欲人勿知，莫若勿为”；今通行说法为后人改写。

pinyin: yī fēn jià qián yī fēn huò
literal: one · portion · price · one · portion · goods
natural: you get what you pay for

meaning.en: The quality of goods matches their price.
meaning.zh: 东西的质量和价格成正比，价钱高质量好，价钱低质量差。

equivalents: you get what you pay for
you pay for quality

examples.zh: 一分价钱一分货，便宜的鞋穿几次就坏了。
examples.en: You get what you pay for; cheap shoes fall apart after a few wears.

examples.zh: 一分价钱一分货，这家店贵但质量真好。
examples.en: This shop is dear but the quality shows; you get what you pay for.

usage.en: Shopping talk; also used by sellers to justify price.
usage.zh: 购物时常说，卖家也用它解释价格。
